# ConsoleService

- Inherits [`Instance`](instance.md)
- A **service**: get it with `game:GetService("ConsoleService")`
- **Not creatable**: it cannot be created with `Instance.new`

The console of a server that runs with no window, and the game's own commands in it.

A dedicated server reads lines from its standard input: `help`, `status`, `players`, `kick`, `ban`, `unban`, `say`, `save` and `stop` are the engine's, and a game adds its own with `Register`. A line runs between two ticks, never during one, so a command that changes the world is an input like a player's. Its answer goes to the standard output and to the log.

Only the server has a console. A client, or a script on the client's side of a machine that hosts, that calls one of these methods gets an error.

This page lists the members this class declares. Inherited members are
listed on the page of the class that declares them.

## Methods

### `ExecuteAsync(line: string): string`

This method yields: the calling thread waits until it completes.

Runs `line` as the server's own console would, with every permission, and returns what the command answered. Raises when the command failed. Yields until the command has finished: a line runs between ticks.

### `Register(name: string, spec: { Description: string?, Parameters: { { Name: string, Type: string, Optional: boolean? } }?, Permission: number? }, callback: (caller: { Local: boolean, Name: string, Key: string, Permission: number }, ...any) -> any)`

Adds the command `name` to the console. `name` is one lowercase word, and none of the engine's own. Registering a name again replaces it, as a hot reload does.

`spec.Parameters` lists what the command takes, in order: each has a `Name` and a `Type` (`"string"`, `"number"`, `"boolean"` or `"Player"`), and the `Optional` ones come last. A word left over at the end goes to the last `string` parameter, so `announce Doors open at noon` gives the whole sentence. A `Player` is written as their name, their `UserId` or the start of their `PublicKey`. A line that does not fit is answered with the command's usage, and `callback` is not called.

`spec.Permission`, 0 to 3, is who may run it: 2 when absent. The local console is 3. `spec.Description` is shown by `help`; it may be a key of the game's own catalog.

`callback` runs on a thread of its own, on the server, between ticks. Its first argument is who ran it, then the parameters, `nil` for an optional one left out. What it returns is shown to whoever ran it; an error it raises is shown the same way and does not stop the server. It may yield, and the console takes the next line meanwhile.

### `Unregister(name: string)`

Takes the command `name` out of the console. Nothing happens if there is none.
